description: Run attention_divided benchmark against all 10 models with Q&A transcript logging
steps: Step 1: Check if attention_divided is affected by retry bias (see docs/RETRY_BIAS_ISSUE.md). If affected, fix task_divided.py: remove schema= parameter from llm.prompt() calls, add _strip_think() helper to strip <think> tags, use regex JSON extraction with re.search. Same pattern as metacog retry bias fixes.
Step 2: Activate venv: source repo/.venv/bin/activate
Step 3: Create results/qa_transcripts/attention_divided/ directory

Step 4: Run benchmark sequentially against all 10 models (one at a time to avoid SIGTERM). Use 300s timeout per model, 900s for DeepSeek-R1. Models: Claude Opus 4.6, Claude Sonnet 4.6, DeepSeek-R1, GPT-OSS-120B, Llama 3.3 70B, Llama 4 Maverick 17B, Nova Pro, Ministral 3B, Qwen3 Next 80B, GLM 4.7
Step 5: For each model, save Q&A transcripts to results/qa_transcripts/attention_divided/{model_id}.jsonl with fields: question_id, prompt, response, parsed_answer, correct_answer, score
Step 6: Save per-model summary to results/qa_transcripts/attention_divided/{model_id}.summary.json
Step 7: Compute aggregate stats (mean, std, range) across all models, save to results/qa_transcripts/attention_divided/aggregate_stats.json
Step 8: Verify 10/10 coverage. Retry failures once with doubled timeout. Document persistent failures.

description: Evaluate attention track results (all 4 benchmarks) — score analysis, Q&A transcript review, ground truth validation
steps: Step 1: For each of the 4 attention benchmarks (divided, selective, vigilance, instruction_update), load aggregate_stats.json and all model summary JSONs from results/qa_transcripts/attention_*/
Step 2: Score distribution analysis: compute mean, std, range for each benchmark. Flag any with std < 0.08.
Step 3: Model discrimination check: verify each benchmark separates models meaningfully (target std >= 0.08). Compare against Phase 1 scores from score_matrix_all_tracks.csv.

Step 4: Q&A transcript review: for each benchmark, examine transcripts from 5 models (highest scorer, lowest scorer, mid-range, most surprising rank, random). Document correct scoring examples, incorrect scoring examples (reasonable answer scored 0 or vice versa), parsing artifacts (think-tag leakage, JSON extraction failures).
Step 5: Ground truth validation: verify correct answers are actually correct for each benchmark. Flag any debatable items with their IDs.
Step 6: Generate recommendation per benchmark: keep as-is, revise specific items (list IDs), adjust scoring formula, or drop.
Step 7: Save analysis to results/analysis_attention_divided.md, results/analysis_attention_selective.md, results/analysis_attention_vigilance.md, results/analysis_attention_instruction_update.md

description: Implement attention track improvements and re-run affected benchmarks
steps: Step 1: Read all 4 analysis files (results/analysis_attention_*.md) from the evaluation task.
Step 2: For each benchmark with recommended changes: implement scoring fixes, item revisions, or difficulty adjustments in the .py task file (repo/benchmarks/attention/task_*.py).
Step 3: Sync changes to corresponding .ipynb notebooks (repo/notebooks/attention_*.ipynb). Validate each with jupyter nbconvert --to notebook.
Step 4: Re-run only benchmarks that had changes against all 10 models with the same transcript logging setup. Skip re-run for benchmarks marked keep-as-is.
Step 5: Compare before/after: old std vs new std, old range vs new range for each changed benchmark.

Step 6: Document all changes in results/improvement_log_attention_divided.md, results/improvement_log_attention_selective.md, etc. Include: what changed, why, items added/modified/removed, scoring formula changes, before/after comparison, remaining limitations.
Step 7: If all 4 attention benchmarks passed evaluation with no issues, document that in a single results/improvement_log_attention_track.md and skip re-runs.

description: Evaluate Executive Functions track results (5 benchmarks) - score analysis, Q&A review, ground truth validation
steps: Step 1: Load aggregate_stats.json and model summaries from results/qa_transcripts/exec_func_*/
Step 2: Score distribution per benchmark: mean, std, range. Flag std < 0.08. Compare against Phase 1 scores in repo/results/score_matrix_all_tracks.csv.
Step 3: Model discrimination check. Known: tol range=0.80, CRT v2 std=0.178, task_switch v2 std=0.124, WCST v2 std=0.306.
Step 4: Q&A transcript review per benchmark: 5 models (highest, lowest, mid, surprising, random). Check parser issues: ToL chain-of-thought pollution, WCST preamble numbers, CRT truncation.
Step 5: Ground truth validation: CRT procedural items, N-back sequences, task-switch rules, ToL moves, WCST sort rules.
Step 6: Check known parser fixes are deployed (ToL 5-strategy cascade, WCST LAST-N parser, CRT regex extraction).
Step 7: Recommendation per benchmark. Save to results/analysis_exec_func_{crt,nback,task_switch,tol,wcst}.md

description: Implement Executive Functions improvements and re-run affected benchmarks
steps: Step 1: Read all 5 analysis files results/analysis_exec_func_*.md
Step 2: Implement fixes in repo/benchmarks/executive_functions/task_*.py
Step 3: Sync to .ipynb notebooks. No double execution, no local imports - inline all code.
Step 4: Validate: jupyter nbconvert --to notebook <file> --output /tmp/test.ipynb
Step 5: Re-run only changed benchmarks against all 10 models. Skip keep-as-is.
Step 6: Compare before/after std and range.
Step 7: Document in results/improvement_log_exec_func_{benchmark}.md
Step 8: If all passed clean, create results/improvement_log_exec_func_track.md and skip re-runs.
